title: The AI Mirror: How to Reclaim Our Humanity in an Age of Machine Thinking

description.main: A philosopher's argument that contemporary AI works as a mirror of human thought and data rather than as an independent mind. Vallor reads the technology through the history of philosophy and proposes designing it around human flourishing and care.
description.extended:
A philosophical case that today's AI systems reflect human data and habits back at us, and that mistaking the reflection for a mind distorts how we build and use them.

Vallor builds the book on the mirror metaphor. AI reflects individuals and societies, reproduces existing inequalities, and shows a flattering image of its own benefits. She opens with the case of Blake Lemoine, the Google engineer who took the LaMDA chatbot to be sentient, and argues he was in effect talking to himself. She traces the misconceptions behind this to classical philosophy, including Plato's separation of the technician from society and Aristotle's exclusion of care-work from virtue, and argues for designing technology around human flourishing, care and moral education. Oxford University Press published the hardcover in 2024.

Shannon Vallor is Baillie Gifford Professor in the Ethics of Data and Artificial Intelligence at the University of Edinburgh. Her earlier book, Technology and the Virtues: A Philosophical Guide to a Future Worth Wanting (2018), applied virtue ethics to technology, drawing on Confucian and Buddhist as well as Western traditions.
